correctness.rationale: Exact tensor reproducing kernel splits into a support-\(k\) squarefree chaos and an \(L^1\)-remainder \(O(d^{(k-1)/2})\) uniform over evaluation points. For a triangular evaluation sequence of energy \(R_d^2/d\to\rho>0\), bounded-array CLT and Newton power-sum identities yield normalized kth elementary symmetric term converging to \(H_k(Z)/k!\), while a universal \(L^2\) bound \(1/k!\) gives uniform integrability. For \(\rho=0\) use the exact L2 inequality. Compact subsequence arguments give sharp norm and if-and-only-if asymptotic extremizer criterion. Selfadjoint symmetric kernel gives identical \(L^1\) and \(L^\infty\) norms. Standalone direct kernel comparisons: 1281 passed for 3 marginals, \(k=3,4\), \(d=2,3,4\); finite checks do not replace analytic proof.

value.rationale: Exact worst-case \(L^1/L^\infty\) amplification is a natural stability invariant for truncating product-measure polynomial chaos and is distinct from \(L^2\) orthogonality or sampling guarantees. The all-fixed-higher-degree family gives precise Hermite oscillation coefficients, works for arbitrary asymmetric or discrete compact marginals, and supplies a complete if-and-only-if geometric characterization of asymptotic maximizing evaluations. Neither a single special numerical constant nor a trivial degree-two restatement: it identifies a universal asymptotic mechanism across every fixed \(k\ge3\) with practical consequences for worst-case inputs. It intentionally excludes unmotivated finite corrections or unproved growing-degree claims.
